zoe (docs): Quick bug report: the /api-keys reference shows `expires_at` as an RFC3339 string in examples, but the runtime returns a unix epoch integer in responses. Caught by a customer test. Opening a docs PR to straighten examples and add a migration note. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3891

michael (eng-api): Confirmed. We recently changed storage to epoch ints for performance reasons but OpenAPI example wasn't updated. Runtime accepts both formats on create (we parse either) but responses are canonicalized to integer epoch. Docs should show the canonical integer and call out create-time acceptability of RFC3339 strings for backward compatibility.

harpreet (sdk): Our Python and JS SDKs currently surface `expires_at` as a datetime object (parsing RFC3339), which will break for integers. I'll push SDK patches to accept both epoch ints and RFC3339 strings and normalize to a datetime object in the client. Will add code snippet for users: `new Date(resp.expires_at * 1000)` for integer case.

dana (docs-review): A couple of nits: 1) update the OpenAPI examples and the example response block; 2) add a short migration section titled "expires_at format change" with sample curl old->new; 3) ensure code fences show language and canonical header `Authorization` casing.

zoe (docs): Will update curl/python/js snippets, OpenAPI example, and add migration callout. Draft migration example:
```bash
# old (RFC3339 string)
curl -X GET $URL -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"expires_at": "2026-06-01T12:00:00Z"}'
# new (epoch seconds)
curl -X GET $URL -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"expires_at": 1717214400}'
```

harpreet (sdk): I'll also add an SDK helper `parseExpiry(resp.expires_at)` in the JS client and update README snippet showing both. I'll link the SDK PR from the docs once ready. ETA: later today.

michael (eng-api): Note for docs: when both `expires_at` and `ttl_seconds` are present, `ttl_seconds` takes precedence for create-time semantics. Please add that to migration note to avoid confusion.

dana (docs-review): Looks good. One extra test suggestion: QA should post a key with RFC3339 string and verify the response `expires_at` is returned as epoch int. Add that to PR description.

ci-bot: docs-ci: running lint and examples check... (warning: missing language for one code fence)

zoe (docs): Fixed code fences and pushed PR changes. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3891

ci-bot: docs-ci ✅ build passed. Deploy preview: https://deploy-preview-3891--redwood-docs.netlify.app/reference/api-keys#responses

zoe (docs): Merging after CI green. Will update the docs changelog with the migration note and link the SDK PR when Harpreet's ready. Thanks all! :white_check_mark:
